note: DACI decisions of record. High authority, long-lived until explicitly superseded or reversed.
Ratified policy documents (status=approved). Authoritative for their domain; drafts do not count.
Finance GL. System of record for recognized revenue/ARR; figures settle monthly.
Human resources system of record for titles, department, employment status.
Identity/access entitlements from the quarterly access review.
Operational truth (incidents, uptime). Authoritative in the moment but decays within hours-to-days; stale status is not current status.
Current product specification. Authoritative for behavior when the section is current, not deprecated.
Customer-facing KB. Useful and usually current, but a doc can lag the spec; older page_history revisions are superseded.
Internal strategy write-ups. Informative on options, but they argue direction rather than set it.
RFCs and proposals for discussion. Low authority by design — a proposal is not a decision.
Informal chat/email discussion. Low authority, short-lived; captures intent, not record.
Email correspondence. Low authority for facts; may carry unverified titles or figures.
Third-party analyst notes written from outside with imperfect information. Lowest authority; frequently wrong on internal facts.
Press/news mentions. Lowest authority; round outside estimates, not internal records.
